proposed_widenings.name: feature_upgrade
proposed_widenings.justification: Greater Divine Intervention does not activate independently. It augments the option set of Divine Intervention (cleric L10): when the player uses that feature, they may now additionally choose Wish. No ClassFeatureMechanics family models 'conditionally extends another feature's option set when that feature is invoked'. Forcing it into the activation family would fabricate a standalone activation that does not exist in the SRD.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you use your Divine Intervention feature, you can choose Wish when you select a spell.

proposed_widenings.name: RestResetCadence: rolled_long_rests
proposed_widenings.justification: The penalty reset cadence when Wish is chosen is '2d4 Long Rests' — a dice-rolled count of long rests, not a fixed number and not any existing cadence variant. RestResetCadence is a closed union of fixed rest categories with no slot for a DiceExpr-parameterized count.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can't use Divine Intervention again until you finish 2d4 Long Rests

proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureEffect: grant_spell_access
proposed_widenings.justification: The new capability is access to the Wish spell via the Divine Intervention invocation path. ClassFeatureEffect only contains grant_extra_action and heal_hp. The v4 atom grant_spell_access exists in the taxonomy but has no corresponding surface variant in ClassFeatureEffect.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can choose Wish when you select a spell

notes: Three distinct gaps: (1) primary structural gap — no family for a feature that conditionally augments another feature's option set at invocation time, with a different reset penalty; (2) surface gap — RestResetCadence needs a rolled_long_rests variant parameterized by DiceExpr; (3) surface gap — ClassFeatureEffect needs a grant_spell_access variant referencing a named spell id. No .dhall or .json authored: forcing this into activation would require fabricating an independent activation cost and effect that the SRD does not describe.
